planner.question: Can a compositional algebraic measure yield an unconditional lower bound for arbitrary fan-in-two SAT selector circuits, beyond fixed-partition rank?
planner.strategy: Compute full multilinear degree by source sign-flip orbit symmetry and transfer to nonlinear gate count.
planner.alternative: Extend orbit argument to prime-domain constraint pools and test the degree ceiling against small circuits.
planner.stop_rule: Do not promote a linear bound in selector length to a superpolynomial separation.
literature_leads: Prior MathOS universal selector and rank compression; classical multilinear Boolean polynomial degree and finite p-group orbit counting. No novelty claim.

construct.claim: The full Boolean selector function has degree N over GF2 and every binary circuit computing it requires at least N-1 nonaffine gates.
construct.scope: Nonempty sign-invariant normalized non-tautological clause pool; unrestricted fan-out and reuse, fixed fan-in-two basis.
construct.derivation: Orbit parity of satisfiable subsets leaves only empty subset; reverse substitution of AND gates increases multilinear degree at most one per gate.
unresolved_steps: Superpolynomial lower bound for the same fixed NP-complete family.
candidate_tests: Union parity polynomial, direct Möbius transforms, circuit degree distributions.

alternative.claim: Prime-domain translation-invariant nontrivial constraint pools have full selector coefficient (-1)^N over GF(p), while maximal degree alone permits linear-size circuits.
alternative.scope: Prime p, coordinate translation group, Boolean selector bits; no identically true constraints.
alternative.derivation: Orbit sizes divisible by p except fixed subsets; nonempty invariant subset infeasible; AND of N bits attains full degree with N-1 gates.
unresolved_steps: A stronger compositional measure with a noncircular superpolynomial bound.
candidate_tests: Prime-domain signed coefficient enumeration and compact AND controls.

objections: Linear in selector length is not a separation.
Full degree can be achieved by a linear-size circuit.
Arbitrary subpools need not be sign invariant.
counterexample_candidates: AND_N attains maximal degree and exact linear gate count; asymmetric clause pool lacks orbit theorem.
critic.equivalence_audit: Exact full coefficient and gate substitution invariant; distinguish selector count from source models.
critic.barrier_audit: No superpolynomial general circuit bound or P versus NP resolution.
